name: Cala Iris
hero_subtitle: Charming fishing village and park-coast gateway along the Al Hoceima National Park shoreline.

overview.title: Gateway to the park shore
overview.p1: Cala Iris is a small, picturesque fishing settlement on the rugged edge of Al Hoceima National Park — serving as an ideal base for relaxing by the water or exploring further along the dramatic cliff coast.
overview.p2: While the local cove itself is relatively modest, the true appeal lies in its breathtaking surroundings: rolling park hills behind, the sparkling Mediterranean ahead, and access to coastal walks or boat excursions toward wilder, hidden inlets.
overview.p3: Be sure to arrange your transport in advance. It pairs exceptionally well with Torres de Alcalá for an unforgettable full-day exploration of the national park shoreline.

q1.question: How far is Cala Iris from Al Hoceima?
q1.answer: It is located west along the coast — be sure to confirm the estimated drive time with your transport provider.

q2.question: Is there a major resort at Cala Iris?
q2.answer: No — it maintains an authentic, village-scale atmosphere rather than a heavily commercialized resort strip.

q3.question: Can I continue exploring deeper into the national park?
q3.answer: Yes, local fishermen offer boat trips and guided coastal walks when weather and sea conditions permit.

q4.question: What are the food options available?
q4.answer: Dining choices are quite simple; it is recommended to pack extra water and light snacks for longer park excursions.

q5.question: Is it worth visiting without taking a boat?
q5.answer: Definitely, purely for the peaceful landscape and quiet cove experience, though boats help unlock the more remote cliff scenery.
